note: All 237 pivots are Hippocratic medical/gynaecological prose. Partners are mostly Cato Agr. recipes, plus Plautus, Lucretius, AV/RV, Avestan and ORV. Nearly all bundles hold generic co-occurrences (wine/give/drink, ordinal + month, rub/grind). Considered and rejected: (1) γλυκύς/μέλι ~ dulcis/mel ('sweeter than honey': comparative + ablatival standard in Homer Il. 1.249, 18.109 and Plautus Asin. 614; the attributive type in Lucretius 1.938/947). It is a cognate pair, but no Hippocratic slab passage carries the collocation and the figure is cross-linguistically generic. (2) δίδωμι + πίνω infinitive ~ Cato do + bibo infinitive: exact cognates in the same prescriptive syntax, but trivial and generic. (3) οἶνος μέλας αὐστηρός ~ uinum nigrum austerum: the colour terms are not cognate and austerus is a Greek loan. (4) Seventh/eighth-month birth: shared subject matter, not phraseology. No claims.
